regions.name: Dolores Plaza
teach: Part 2: Father Hidalgo and Mexican Independence. Mexicans were unhappy with Spanish rule: men born in Spain got the best jobs, high taxes paid for wars in Europe, and they were ruled by someone far away in Europe.
Father Hidalgo was a Catholic priest in the town of Dolores. He was born in 1753.
The Grito de Dolores happened on September 16, 1810: his call for the people of Mexico to rise up against Spanish rule.
Problems that hurt his army: lack of discipline, no military training, and it failed to capture Mexico City.
Hidalgo was captured and executed in 1811. Mexico finally won independence in 1821. He is the Father of Mexican Independence.

merchant.name: Plaza trader
merchant.hello: Welcome to Dolores! Everything on my table has a story.

goods.name: Bell of Dolores
goods.fact: On September 16, 1810, in the town of Dolores, Father Hidalgo gave the Grito de Dolores: his call for the people of Mexico to rise up against Spanish rule.

goods.name: Priest's Candle
goods.fact: Father Hidalgo was a Catholic priest, born in 1753. He was captured and executed in 1811. Mexico won independence in 1821, and he is called the Father of Mexican Independence.

regions.name: Big Picture Mesa
teach: Part 1: The Big Picture. The Seven Years' War (1754-1763) is also called the French and Indian War.
After the war, Great Britain gained Canada and all land east of the Mississippi River. Spain got New Orleans and all French land west of it. France lost; the United States did not exist yet.
Rubí suggested closing all missions in Texas except Goliad and San Antonio.
The Louisiana Purchase: 1803, President Thomas Jefferson, $15 million, doubled the size of the United States.
Map of 1803: 1 = Oregon Territory, 2 = British North America, 3 = United States, 4 = Louisiana Purchase, 5 = New Spain.

merchant.name: Mesa fur trader
merchant.hello: I have traded on both sides of the Mississippi. Ask me who owned what.

goods.name: Beaver Pelt
goods.fact: The Seven Years' War (1754-1763) is also called the French and Indian War. After it, Great Britain gained Canada and all land east of the Mississippi River. Spain got New Orleans and the French land west of it.

goods.name: Louisiana Receipt
goods.fact: The Louisiana Purchase: in 1803 President Thomas Jefferson paid $15 million, and it doubled the size of the United States.

regions.name: Filibuster Trail
teach: Part 3: Filibusters. The four parts: from a foreign country (not Spanish); came to fight the government; wanted land and power; wanted personal gain (wealth).
All four must be true. If one is missing the answer is NO, and the missing part is the reason.
Filibusters: Philip Nolan, Augustus Magee, James Long.
NO: Father Hidalgo (not foreign, no personal gain). Moses Austin and Stephen F. Austin (did not fight the government; they asked permission).

merchant.name: Trail horse trader
merchant.hello: Careful on this trail. Some men ride into Texas without asking anyone.

goods.name: Mustang Charm
goods.fact: A filibuster has all four parts: from a foreign country, came to fight the government, wanted land and power, and wanted personal gain. Philip Nolan, Augustus Magee and James Long were filibusters.

goods.name: Torn Flag
goods.fact: If one of the four parts is missing, the answer is NO. Father Hidalgo was not a filibuster: he was not foreign and wanted no personal gain. Moses and Stephen F. Austin were not: they asked permission and did not fight the government.

regions.name: Austin's Colony
teach: Part 4: Empresarios. An empresario was a land agent who brought settlers into Texas in exchange for land.
1820: Spain opened Texas to foreign settlers. They had to be Catholic (or convert), be hard-working and become citizens.
Mexico wanted settlers to protect Texas from United States expansion and hostile Indians. Anglo-Americans came for cheap land and to escape debt.
1821: Moses Austin was promised a contract for 300 Catholic families but died. Stephen F. Austin took it over: the Father of Texas. His first settlers: the Old Three Hundred.
Martín De León: native Mexican empresario; his colony was the only one settled mainly by Mexican families.

merchant.name: Land office clerk
merchant.hello: Looking for land? Here you need a contract first.

goods.name: Land Grant
goods.fact: An empresario was a land agent who brought settlers into Texas in exchange for land. Stephen F. Austin, the Father of Texas, took over the contract of his father Moses Austin. His first settlers were the Old Three Hundred.

goods.name: Settler's Axe
goods.fact: When Spain opened Texas to foreign settlers in 1820, they had to be Catholic (or convert), be hard-working and become citizens. Anglo-Americans came for cheap land and to escape debt.

regions.name: Word Mill
teach: Part 7: Vocabulary. militia: citizens acting as a military force. centralist: power in the national government. federalist: power shared between states and national government.
survey: measure the boundaries of land. pioneer: travels to unclaimed territory to settle. depression: low economic activity, high unemployment.
diminish: become smaller. prime: top quality, the best. presidio: Spanish fort protecting missions. mission: religious settlement run by Catholic priests.
Anglo American: white, English-speaking settler from the United States. land grant: land given by a government in exchange for settling it.

merchant.name: Mill storekeeper
merchant.hello: Words are my trade. Each of these teaches you two.

goods.name: Surveyor's Rule
goods.fact: To survey is to measure the boundaries of land. A land grant is land given by a government in exchange for settling it.

goods.name: Model Presidio
goods.fact: A presidio was a Spanish fort that protected the missions. A mission was a religious settlement run by Catholic priests.

regions.name: Old Camino Real
teach: Earlier this week. Rubí: Spain lacked the wealth and power to defend all of Texas. The 13 colonies declared independence in 1776.
New Orleans was the port for Mississippi River trade. Lewis and Clark explored the Louisiana Purchase, which made the U.S. Texas's neighbor.
Peter Ellis Bean was Nolan's companion, captured by the Spanish. Jean Lafitte was the pirate on Galveston Island. Barr: NO, he did not fight the government.

merchant.name: Camino Real peddler
merchant.hello: I have walked this road all week. I remember everything on it.

goods.name: Pirate's Parrot
goods.fact: Jean Lafitte was the pirate on Galveston Island. Peter Ellis Bean was Philip Nolan's companion, captured by the Spanish.

goods.name: New Orleans Anchor
goods.fact: New Orleans was the port for Mississippi River trade. Lewis and Clark explored the Louisiana Purchase, which made the United States Texas's neighbor.

regions.name: Clock Tower
teach: Part 6: Timeline. 1753 Father Hidalgo is born. 1803 the Louisiana Purchase. 1810 the Grito de Dolores. 1811 Hidalgo is captured and executed. 1821 Mexico wins independence from Spain.
Grito to independence: 1821 - 1810 = 11 years.
Also: 1763 Seven Years' War ends, 1776 U.S. independence, 1820 Spain opens Texas to settlers, 1821 the Austin contract.

merchant.name: Clockmaker
merchant.hello: Tick, tock. Dates are easier when you can hold them.

goods.name: Eleven-Year Hourglass
goods.fact: From the Grito de Dolores in 1810 to Mexican independence in 1821 is 11 years: 1821 - 1810 = 11.

goods.name: Timeline Calendar
goods.fact: In order: 1753 Father Hidalgo is born, 1803 the Louisiana Purchase, 1810 the Grito de Dolores, 1811 Hidalgo is captured and executed, 1821 Mexico wins independence from Spain.

regions.name: Hall of the Republic
teach: Part 5: Compare. Filibusters came without permission to fight the government for land, power and wealth. The government fought them.
Empresarios came with permission and had contracts to bring settlers. Mexico welcomed them to help protect Texas.

merchant.name: Notary of the Republic
merchant.hello: Permission is everything. I stamp the papers that prove it.

goods.name: Stamped Contract
goods.fact: Empresarios came with permission and had contracts to bring settlers; Mexico welcomed them to help protect Texas. Filibusters came without permission to fight the government for land, power and wealth.

questions.q: Which was a reason Mexicans were unhappy with Spanish rule?
choices: People born in Spain got the best jobs
Spain refused to collect any taxes
Spain let Mexicans elect the king
Spain gave every family free land

questions.review: Men born in Spain got the best jobs

choices: Men who were born in Spain
Men who were born in Mexico

questions.q: Why did Spain raise taxes so high in Mexico?
choices: To pay for its wars in Europe
questions.explain: Spain was fighting wars in Europe and made its colonies pay for them. Mexicans paid, but got nothing back.
questions.review: High taxes paid for wars in Europe

variants.q: High taxes made Mexicans angry because the money was spent on...

questions.q: Mexicans were ruled by a king who lived...
questions.explain: The king was in Spain, an ocean away. People in Mexico had no say in the rules made for them.
questions.review: Ruled by someone far away in Europe

variants.q: Three reasons Mexicans were unhappy: Spanish-born men got the best jobs, high taxes for Europe's wars, and...
choices: being ruled by someone far away in Europe

questions.q: After the Seven Years' War, who gained Canada and all land east of the Mississippi River?
questions.explain: Great Britain won the war, so it took Canada and the land east of the Mississippi. France LOST this land. The United States did not exist yet.

questions.q: North America in 1803: what is the name of Region 1 (the gold one)?

variants.q: Which region is the far north, the land Britain took from France? Find it on the map.

questions.q: North America in 1803: what is the name of Region 3 (the gold one)?

questions.explain: Region 5 is the southwest and Mexico, touching the Gulf of Mexico: New Spain. Texas was part of it.

questions.q: A white, English-speaking settler from the United States who is not Hispanic: (from the word bank)
questions.explain: Anglo Americans were the English-speaking settlers from the United States.
questions.review: Anglo American: a white, english-speaking settler from the united states who is not hispanic

variants.q: An English-speaking settler from the United States in Texas was called an...

questions.q: Land given by a government, often in exchange for settling it:
questions.explain: A land grant is land the government gives you. Empresarios and settlers got them.
questions.review: land grant: land given by a government, often in exchange for settling it

variants.q: The government gives a settler land in exchange for living on it. That is a...

questions.q: Rubí said Spain did not have the ______ or ______ to defend all its claims in Texas.
questions.explain: Spain's empire was too big and too costly, so Rubí said to pull back to what it could defend.
questions.review: Rubí: not enough wealth or power

questions.q: In what year did the 13 colonies declare independence from Great Britain?
questions.explain: 1776. That is when the United States began, 13 years after the Seven Years' War ended.

questions.q: Why was New Orleans so important to the United States?
choices: It was the port for trade down the Mississippi River
It had the biggest gold mine
It was the capital of New Spain
questions.explain: Farmers shipped goods down the Mississippi and out through New Orleans, so the U.S. needed that port.
questions.review: New Orleans = port on the Mississippi

questions.q: Which expedition explored the Louisiana Purchase?
questions.explain: Jefferson sent Lewis and Clark to explore the new land.

questions.q: Why did the Louisiana Purchase worry Spain about Texas?
choices: The United States was now right next door to Texas
questions.explain: Louisiana touched Texas, so Americans were now on the border, and some (filibusters) crossed it.

questions.q: Who was Philip Nolan's companion who was captured by the Spanish?
questions.explain: Peter Ellis Bean was with Nolan and spent years as a Spanish prisoner.

questions.q: Which filibuster was a pirate on Galveston Island?
questions.explain: Jean Lafitte ran his pirate base from Galveston Island.

questions.q: Barr was a trader with Spanish permission. Filibuster or NO?
questions.explain: NO. Like Moses Austin, Barr was not prepared to fight the government.

questions.q: After the Seven Years' War, France was...
choices: no longer a colonial power in North America
the owner of all land east of the Mississippi
questions.explain: France lost Canada to Britain and gave Louisiana to Spain, so it had nothing left on the mainland.
questions.review: France lost its North American lands

questions.q: Which government decided who counted as a filibuster in Texas before 1821?
questions.explain: Texas belonged to Spain until 1821, so 'filibuster' is how the Spanish saw these invaders.

questions.q: Put these in order, earliest first.
items: Father Hidalgo is captured and executed
questions.explain: 1753 born, 1803 Louisiana Purchase, 1810 Grito, 1811 executed, 1821 independence.

variants.q: Again, earliest first. (Hint: 1753, 1803, 1810, 1811, 1821.)
items: Father Hidalgo is captured and executed

questions.q: Put these years in the order the events on the study guide happened: Hidalgo born, Louisiana Purchase, Grito, Hidalgo executed, Mexico independent.
questions.explain: Born 1753, Purchase 1803, Grito 1810, executed 1811, independent 1821.

questions.q: Earliest first: the big picture.
items: Seven Years' War ends (Britain and Spain gain land)
Spain opens Texas to foreign settlers
Stephen F. Austin takes over his father's contract
Seven Years' War ends (Britain and Spain gain land)
Spain opens Texas to foreign settlers
Stephen F. Austin takes over his father's contract

questions.q: How many years passed between the Grito de Dolores and Mexican independence? (number)
questions.explain: 1821 - 1810 = 11 years. Subtract the Grito year from the independence year.

variants.q: The Grito was in 1810. Mexico won independence in 1821. 1821 - 1810 = ?

questions.q: Hidalgo gave the Grito in 1810 and was executed in 1811. How many years later was that? (number)
questions.explain: 1811 - 1810 = 1. His revolt lasted only about a year, but the fight he started went on for ten more.

questions.q: Which happened in the SAME year that Mexico won independence (1821)?
choices: Moses Austin was promised his contract
questions.explain: 1821 is a double year: Mexico became independent AND Moses Austin was promised the contract his son took over.

questions.q: Which event came FIRST?
questions.explain: 1803 is the earliest of the four.

questions.q: How did FILIBUSTERS come to Texas?
choices: Without permission, to fight the government for land, power and wealth
With a contract, to bring settler families
As Spanish soldiers, to guard presidios
questions.explain: Filibusters came uninvited and armed. That is the big difference from empresarios.

variants.q: Which word pair fits a filibuster?

questions.q: How did EMPRESARIOS come to Texas?
choices: With permission and land contracts, to bring settlers
questions.explain: Empresarios asked first and had legal contracts. They brought families, not armies.

variants.q: Which word pair fits an empresario?

questions.q: How did the Spanish government respond to filibusters?
choices: It fought them: they were captured, driven out or killed
questions.explain: Filibusters were enemies. Nolan was killed, Bean was jailed, Long was captured.

questions.q: How did the government respond to empresarios?
choices: It welcomed them, because their settlers would help protect Texas
It sent the army to stop them
questions.explain: Loyal settlers filled empty Texas and guarded it, so the government welcomed empresarios and paid them in land.

questions.q: A man from Kentucky leads 100 armed men into Texas to take land and rule it. He is...
questions.explain: Foreign, fighting the government, wants land and power for himself: all four parts.

questions.q: A man from Missouri signs a contract with the government and brings 300 families who become Catholic citizens. He is...
questions.explain: Contract, permission, settlers: an empresario (this is Stephen F. Austin).

questions.q: Father Hidalgo AND James Long both fought the Spanish government. Why is only Long a filibuster?
choices: Long was a foreigner who wanted personal gain; Hidalgo was neither
Hidalgo was foreign and Long was not
questions.explain: Hidalgo was from New Spain and fought for his people's freedom. Long came from the U.S. for land and power.

questions.q: In 1803, Texas was part of which region on the map?
questions.explain: Texas belonged to Spain, so it was in New Spain (Region 5), right beside the Louisiana Purchase.

questions.q: Put the two 'Fathers' with the right title.
choices: Hidalgo: Father of Mexican Independence. Stephen F. Austin: Father of Texas.
Hidalgo: Father of Texas. Stephen F. Austin: Father of Mexican Independence.
Moses Austin: Father of Texas. Hidalgo: Father of Mexican Independence.
Hidalgo: Father of Texas. Martín De León: Father of Mexican Independence.
questions.explain: Hidalgo started Mexico's independence. Stephen F. Austin (the son) built the first Anglo colony in Texas.

questions.q: Who won the Seven Years' War and gained Canada? Great ______.
questions.explain: Great Britain. Not France (France lost) and not America (it did not exist yet).
questions.review: Britain won the Seven Years' War

questions.q: A settler in 1821 says: 'I lost everything in the depression, and land in Texas is cheap.' He is giving reasons why...
choices: Anglo-Americans wanted to move to Texas
questions.explain: Debt and cheap land were the settlers' own reasons. Mexico's reason was protecting Texas.
